How to prepare for current affairs

blocks.text: Indian polity and the Constitution

The General Test paper asks two kinds of general knowledge questions: **static** facts that stay the same for decades, and **current affairs** that depend on recent news. This lesson teaches the static core first, because it is the part you can master completely, and then shows a method for the part that keeps changing. Every fact below is a stable textbook fact; where a number can change with time, it is deliberately left out.

The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950, which is why we celebrate Republic Day on that date. Dr Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly and Dr B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. The Constitution begins with a **Preamble** that describes India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic and promises justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all citizens.

Rights guaranteed to every citizen (and in some cases every person) by Part III of the Constitution, Articles 12 to 35. They can be enforced by going to the Supreme Court (Article 32) or a High Court (Article 226). Examples are equality before law (Article 14), abolition of untouchability (Article 17), protection of life and personal liberty (Article 21) and the right to education for children aged 6 to 14 (Article 21A).

Part IV contains the **Directive Principles of State Policy**. They are guidelines for the government, not enforceable in a court, so they are called non-justiciable. Part IVA, Article 51A, lists the **Fundamental Duties**, added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. The right to property is no longer a Fundamental Right: the 44th Amendment (1978) made it a legal right under Article 300A.

The Union Parliament has three parts: the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. The Lok Sabha is the directly elected lower house with a normal term of five years; a member must be at least 25 years old. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house that is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every two years, each member serves six years, and the minimum age is 30. The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. The minimum age to become President is 35.

Local self-government was strengthened by the 73rd Amendment (Panchayati Raj in villages) and the 74th Amendment (municipalities in towns), both of 1992 and in force from 1993. India is a federal country with a strong Centre: powers are divided into the Union List, State List and Concurrent List.
Remember the ages 25 (Lok Sabha), 30 (Rajya Sabha) and 35 (President). Remember that Fundamental Rights are in Part III, Directive Principles in Part IV and Fundamental Duties in Part IVA.
Geography of India and the world

India lies in the northern and eastern hemispheres. The **Tropic of Cancer** (23.5 degrees north) passes through eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. The **Standard Meridian** of India is 82 degrees 30 minutes east, which passes near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh; Indian Standard Time is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time, because the Earth turns 15 degrees every hour and 82.5 divided by 15 is 5.5.

Physical features worth knowing: the Himalayas in the north, the Northern Plains built by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra systems, the Peninsular Plateau (the Deccan), the Thar Desert in Rajasthan, and the Western and Eastern Ghats along the coasts. Kangchenjunga is the highest peak within India. Rajasthan is the largest state by area and Goa the smallest. Chilika in Odisha is the largest coastal lagoon, and the Sundarbans in West Bengal is the largest mangrove forest. The Ganga rises at the Gangotri glacier. Black soil, ideal for cotton, is found mainly on the Deccan plateau.

World geography: Asia is the largest continent, the Pacific the largest ocean, Mount Everest the highest peak above sea level, the Nile among the longest rivers, and the Mariana Trench the deepest known ocean trench. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.
History: from the Indus cities to Independence

The Indus Valley (Harappan) civilisation, with cities such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, flourished around 2500 BCE and was known for town planning and drainage. Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan empire; his grandson Ashoka gave up war after the Kalinga war and spread Buddhism. The Gupta period is often called the golden age of art and science.

In the medieval period the Delhi Sultanate began in 1206 and the Mughal empire began when Babur won the First Battle of Panipat in 1526. Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri and Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal. British power was established after the Battle of Plassey in 1757.

Chronology questions are easy marks if you attach each event to a decade: 1857 revolt, 1885 Congress, 1900s partition of Bengal, 1919-20 Jallianwala Bagh and Non-Cooperation, 1930 Dandi, 1942 Quit India, 1947 Independence.

blocks.problem: Arrange these in chronological order: Dandi March, Revolt of 1857, Quit India Movement, Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
blocks.solution: Step 1: attach a year to each event from the table. Revolt of 1857 is 1857; Jallianwala Bagh is 1919; Dandi March is 1930; Quit India is 1942. Step 2: sort the years in increasing order: 1857, 1919, 1930, 1942. Step 3: write the events in that order.
blocks.answer: Revolt of 1857, Jallianwala Bagh massacre, Dandi March, Quit India Movement.

blocks.text: Science and technology basics

ISRO, the Indian Space Research Organisation, was formed in 1969 and has its headquarters in Bengaluru. India's first satellite, Aryabhata, was launched in 1975. The Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) was launched in November 2013 and reached Mars orbit in September 2014. Chandrayaan-3 made a soft landing near the Moon's south polar region in August 2023.

Basic science and computing facts: vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, vitamin D deficiency causes rickets, and iodine deficiency causes goitre. One byte is 8 bits. The World Wide Web was proposed by Tim Berners-Lee. The CPU is the brain of a computer and RAM is its short-term working memory. HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol.
Awards, books and authors

The **Bharat Ratna** is India's highest civilian award; next in order come the Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri. The Jnanpith Award honours Indian literature. Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913, the first Asian to win a Nobel Prize, and he also wrote the words and music of India's national anthem.
Important days and institutions

Fixed dates repeat every year: Republic Day 26 January, International Women's Day 8 March, Earth Day 22 April, World Environment Day 5 June, International Yoga Day 21 June, World Population Day 11 July, Independence Day 15 August, Teachers' Day 5 September (birthday of Dr S. Radhakrishnan), Gandhi Jayanti 2 October, United Nations Day 24 October, Children's Day 14 November, World AIDS Day 1 December and Human Rights Day 10 December.

blocks.problem: A question asks: 'Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? (a) UNESCO - Paris (b) WHO - Geneva (c) IMF - New York (d) RBI - Mumbai.' Find the odd pair.
blocks.solution: Check each pair against the headquarters table. UNESCO is in Paris, so (a) is correct. The World Health Organization is in Geneva, so (b) is correct. The International Monetary Fund is in Washington, D.C., not New York, so (c) is wrong. The Reserve Bank of India is in Mumbai, so (d) is correct. The question asks for the pair that is not correctly matched.
blocks.answer: (c) IMF - New York is wrongly matched.

blocks.text: How to prepare for current affairs

Current affairs questions in the General Test usually cover the previous 6 to 12 months, but you cannot memorise a newspaper. Use a system instead. First, read one reliable national newspaper or a monthly digest every day for 20 minutes, and ignore opinion pieces and sports gossip. Second, keep a single notebook with these headings: government schemes and laws, appointments, awards and sports results, summits and treaties, science and space, and places in the news. Third, for every item write the **who, what, where and when** in one line.

The most important habit is to **link each news item to a static fact**. If a new bench of a court or a new organisation is in the news, note the article of the Constitution, the headquarters, the year of founding or the parent body. Examiners like this style because it tests understanding, not just memory. Revise the notebook every Sunday and test yourself with ten quick questions.

Common mistakes: trusting social media forwards, learning a number without its date, confusing a person's old office with the present one, and ignoring the month in which an event happened. If you are not sure whether a fact is still current, check the date of your source before you learn it.

Static GK is learnt once and lasts: Constitution dates, ages, articles, geography, freedom struggle dates, awards, books and headquarters. For current affairs, learn who-what-where-when and tie every item to a static fact.

questions.stem: On which date did the Constitution of India come into force?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949, but it came into force on 26 January 1950, which is why 26 January is celebrated as Republic Day. Independence Day marks 15 August 1947.

optionRationale.1: This is the date of adoption, not of coming into force.
optionRationale.3: This is the date of Independence, before the Constitution existed.
optionRationale.4: This date is close to Gandhi Jayanti and has no link to the Constitution.

questions.objective: Recall the date on which the Constitution came into force

questions.stem: Fundamental Rights are contained in which part of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Part III (Articles 12 to 35) lists the Fundamental Rights. Part IV contains the Directive Principles of State Policy, and Part IVA contains the Fundamental Duties. Parts I and II deal with the Union and its territory and with citizenship.

optionRationale.1: Part I describes the Union and its territory.
optionRationale.3: Part IV is the Directive Principles, not Fundamental Rights.

questions.objective: Locate Fundamental Rights in the Constitution

questions.stem: What is the highest civilian award of India?
questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian honour. The Padma awards rank below it in the order Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri, while the Arjuna Award is a sports award, not a civilian honour of that rank.

optionRationale.2: Padma Vibhushan is the second highest civilian award.
optionRationale.3: Padma Shri is the fourth in order among the civilian awards.
optionRationale.4: The Arjuna Award is given for achievement in sports.

questions.objective: Recall the order of civilian awards

questions.stem: World Environment Day is observed every year on
questions.explanation: World Environment Day falls on 5 June each year. Earth Day is 22 April, International Yoga Day is 21 June and World Population Day is 11 July, so these dates must be learnt as separate facts.
questions.objective: Recall fixed dates of important days

right: III. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam

questions.explanation: Discovery of India was written by Jawaharlal Nehru (IV), Gitanjali by Rabindranath Tagore (I), the Arthashastra by Kautilya (II) and Wings of Fire by A. P. J. Abdul Kalam (III). So the code is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

optionRationale.4: It gives Discovery of India to Kalam and Wings of Fire to Nehru.

questions.objective: Match famous books with their authors

questions.stem: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer crosses Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram, which is a total of eight states. Learn them as a group, because the question may ask the count or ask which state is not on the line.

optionRationale.1: Five misses three of the states on the line.
optionRationale.2: Six misses two of the states on the line.
optionRationale.4: Ten is more than the number of states the line crosses.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Parliament of India.
A. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and is not dissolved.
B. One-third of the members of the Rajya Sabha retire every two years.
C. The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
D. The minimum age for membership of the Lok Sabha is 30 years.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements A, B and C are correct. The Rajya Sabha is never dissolved, a third of its members retire every two years, and the Vice-President chairs it. Statement D is wrong because the minimum age for the Lok Sabha is 25; 30 is the age for the Rajya Sabha.

optionRationale.1: It leaves out C, which is correct.
optionRationale.3: It includes D, which is wrong (the age is 25).
optionRationale.4: It includes D and leaves out B, which is correct.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
Reason (R): The Lok Sabha is directly elected by the people and holds control over government finances, while the Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations on such a bill.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. Because the Lok Sabha represents the people directly and controls money, the Constitution gives it the sole power to introduce Money Bills, and the Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes. So R explains A.

optionRationale.2: R is not just a true remark; it is the reason for A, so option 2 is too weak.
optionRationale.3: A is true, so option 3 cannot be right.
optionRationale.4: A is true and R is also true, so option 4 is wrong.

questions.objective: Explain the Lok Sabha's financial powers

questions.stem: The headquarters of UNESCO is located in
questions.explanation: UNESCO has its headquarters in Paris. Geneva hosts the World Health Organization, New York hosts the United Nations and Washington, D.C. hosts the World Bank and the IMF. A common trap is to pick New York for every international body, so learn each headquarters separately.

optionRationale.1: Geneva is the home of the WHO.
optionRationale.2: New York is the home of the United Nations.
optionRationale.3: Washington, D.C. hosts the World Bank and IMF.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Rabindranath Tagore was the first Asian to win a Nobel Prize.
Reason (R): Rabindranath Tagore wrote the words and music of the national anthem of India.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913, the first Asian to do so, and he also wrote the national anthem. Both statements are true, but writing the anthem has nothing to do with winning the Nobel Prize, so R does not explain A.

optionRationale.1: R is true but it is not the reason for the Nobel Prize, so it is not a correct explanation.
optionRationale.3: A is true, so option 3 is wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so option 4 is wrong.

questions.stem: Which is the correct chronological order of these events: (1) Quit India Movement, (2) Jallianwala Bagh massacre, (3) Dandi March, (4) Revolt of 1857?
questions.explanation: The dates are Revolt of 1857, Jallianwala Bagh 1919, Dandi March 1930 and Quit India 1942. In increasing order this is 4, 2, 3, 1, so the sequence option beginning with 4 and ending with 1 is correct. Always attach years before comparing events.

optionRationale.1: It puts the Dandi March (1930) before Jallianwala Bagh (1919).
optionRationale.3: It puts the Jallianwala Bagh massacre before the Revolt of 1857.
optionRationale.4: It puts Quit India (1942) before the Dandi March (1930).

questions.objective: Arrange freedom struggle events in order

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements.
A. The Directive Principles of State Policy cannot be enforced by a court.
B. The Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment.
C. The right to property is today a Fundamental Right under Part III.
D. Article 17 abolishes untouchability.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: A is correct because Directive Principles are non-justiciable. B is correct because Article 51A was added in 1976. D is correct because Article 17 abolishes untouchability. C is wrong: the 44th Amendment removed the right to property from Part III and made it a legal right under Article 300A.

optionRationale.2: It includes C, which is wrong, and leaves out A.
optionRationale.3: It includes C, which is wrong, and leaves out A.
optionRationale.4: It includes C and leaves out B and D, which are correct.

questions.objective: Separate correct from incorrect constitutional statements

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): The Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest of India, is located in Odisha.
Reason (R): The Sundarbans lie in the delta formed by the Ganga and the Brahmaputra.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans are in West Bengal (and Bangladesh), not in Odisha, so A is false. R is true, because the Sundarbans form on the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta. The correct option is therefore the one saying A is false but R is true.

optionRationale.1: A is false because the Sundarbans are in West Bengal, so options 1 and 2 fail.
optionRationale.2: A is false because the Sundarbans are in West Bengal, so options 1 and 2 fail.
optionRationale.3: R is true, so option 3 fails.

questions.stem: Which one of the following institution-headquarters pairs is NOT correctly matched?
options: Election Commission of India - New Delhi
questions.explanation: The World Bank has its headquarters in Washington, D.C., not Geneva, so this pair is wrongly matched. The RBI is in Mumbai, the Election Commission in New Delhi and ISRO in Bengaluru, so those pairs are correct.

optionRationale.1: This pair is correct, so it is not the answer.
optionRationale.2: This pair is correct, so it is not the answer.
optionRationale.3: This pair is correct, so it is not the answer.

questions.stem: A news item reports that a new body has been set up. Which method of study is best for the General Test?
options: Note who, what, where and when in one line, and link it to a static fact such as its article, parent body or headquarters
Memorise the headline word for word without a date
Skip it because only static questions are asked
Rely on a social media forward for the details
questions.explanation: A short who-what-where-when note with a link to a static fact is accurate, quick to revise and tests understanding. Memorising headlines without a date, skipping current affairs or trusting unverified forwards leads to wrong or outdated answers.

optionRationale.2: Without the date the fact may be out of date.
optionRationale.3: Current affairs questions do appear in the paper.

questions.objective: Apply a method for studying current affairs
